findings.evidence: The instances are defined at lines 46–53 and 173–177; `rg` finds no comparison iff API, while line 210 itself proves refinement by `change sortedParts ν < sortedParts μ`, demonstrating reliance on the private implementation and definitional reduction.
findings.fix: Add appropriately scoped `[simp]` iff lemmas for lexicographic `<` (and `≤` if useful) and dominance `≤`, stated using `μ.parts.sort (· ≥ ·)` and `Dominates`; use these lemmas in `lex_lt_of_strictlyDominates`.
findings.issue: `PartitionLex.partitionLinearOrder` and `DominanceOrder.partitionPartialOrder` lack public `lt`/`le` characterization lemmas, so users cannot reduce partition comparisons to sorted-parts lexicography or `Dominates` without relying on definitional unfolding.

summary: The scoped order instances are exposed without lemmas characterizing their comparison operators, forcing consumers to unfold instance bodies.
